subject: Request: custom availability framework & latency safeguard for DetailCare (MSA/SOW attachments)
messages:
From: James Patel <j.patel@detailcare.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@detailcare.com, m.torres@detailcare.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production readiness and SLA scope for rollout

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. As we prepare to finalize the MSA/SOW and the order form, procurement asked me to collect the specific language and evidence we will need for the availability and latency commitments.

We have two asks from our side:
- A custom availability commitment that reflects our multi-region failover plan (primary region + two DR islands). We expect a 99.95% monthly availability target for the primary region and a documented fallback behavior for DR islands.
- A latency safeguard for tail latency: we need quantile-based SLOs (p95/p99) for 1k-token generation and explicit escalation/backstop in case of repeated breaches.

Can you point us to a proposed addendum (MSA exhibit / order form wording) and the evidence package (monitoring, retention windows, and audit traces) you can provide? Procurement would also like to see what exceptions you can accept and the approvals path.

Attaching a short summary from our side.

[Attachment: detailcare-requested-sla-scope.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks,
James
James Patel
VP, Infrastructure Operations
DetailCare Health

From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: James Patel <j.patel@detailcare.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production readiness and SLA scope for rollout

James — really helpful summary, thanks. We can do a tailored addendum and baked-in order form language to cover both items you outlined. High level plan and the materials we will share: 

1) Proposed SLA addendum (MSA exhibit):
   - Primary availability SLO: 99.95% monthly (per-region).
   - DR/Failover behavior: documented failover playbook + recovery time expectations; DR islands have a committed uplifted latency guard but lower availability SLO (described in the exhibit).
   - Credits and remediation: clear credit schedule tied to per-region monthly availability; separate mechanism for repeated tail-latency regressions.

2) Latency safeguard:
   - Quantile SLOs: p95 and p99 thresholds for 1k-token workloads and an escalation ladder (automated alerts -> ops runbook -> executive notice -> remediation credit).
   - Operational backstops: temporary routing to a higher-throughput model variant or designated dedicated pool when thresholds are breached.

3) Evidence package we can provide:
   - 90-day rolling latency and availability telemetry (per-region)
   - Audit log extracts for request ids (retention window options)
   - Playbook excerpts and runbook ownership

I've attached a first-draft addendum (internal draft) and an evidence matrix. Please review and flag any must-haves from your legal/procurement side. If that looks ok, we can prepare a redline-ready exhibit for your legal team and a DocuSign route for the order form.

Attachments:
- redwood-proposed-sla-addendum-v0.1.pdf
- evidence-matrix-detailcare.xlsx

Next steps: if procurement can circulate suggested edits by EOD Monday we will incorporate and queue a canary order form change for approval. If you prefer, we can also schedule a 30-minute call with our legal/ops to walk through the exhibit.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Production readiness and SLA scope for rollout

Alex / Karthik — looping in Hannah from legal because a few specific redlines will be important for the MSA exhibit. Quick notes based on the draft: 

- Limit the definition of "availability" to the service endpoints used by DetailCare (api.redwood.com + region-specific edges) and add an explicit exclusion for customer-side network interruptions.
- For latency SLOs, prefer a rolling-window definition (30-day calc for p95, 90-day for p99) to reduce noisy variance during the initial ramp.
- Any auto-routing fallback needs to be described as an optional operational mitigation, not an SLA obligation; otherwise it creates an operational dependency that can be invoked as a failure mode.
- Evidence: we should offer a scoped extract of request ids and timestamped trace samples (redact PII) and propose a separate technical addendum describing retention windows and delivery format (CSV/Parquet).

Suggested order-form wording for the credits clause (high level):
- Credits capped at x% of monthly invoice per incident window; aggregated monthly cap; not cumulative across distinct legal entities.

I've left inline comments on the draft addendum (see attachment). We'll aim to keep the document lean to avoid heavy procurement pushback.

[Attachment: redwood-proposed-sla-addendum-v0.1.pdf (PDF) — annotated]

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: James Patel <j.patel@detailcare.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@detailcare.com, m.torres@detailcare.com
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production readiness and SLA scope for rollout

Alex / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the annotated draft. A couple of clarifying points from procurement/legal: 

1) Regional exceptions: we understand the need for different SLOs per-region, but DetailCare requires a documented exception approval path (who signs off internally and what evidence is sufficient). Can Redwood provide an escalation contact and estimated review timeline for exception requests?

2) Evidence delivery: the CSV extract format you mentioned works. We will need that data for audit purposes for up to 12 months. Can you confirm retention options (30/90/365 days) and the export cadence?

3) DocuSign: once legal accepts the redlines we will circulate a route. Please confirm if the order form language needs an explicit MSA amendment reference or if we can attach the exhibit as an SOW-level addendum.

We are ok with the credits cap but need the definitions to be explicit in the exhibit (time windows, measurement method). Also, please include a sample incident timeline demonstrating how a latency breach leads to remediation actions and when credit calculations would start. That will speed our internal approval.

Attachments: none in this reply.

Regards,
James
VP, Infrastructure Operations
DetailCare Health
